newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks slide further, profit-taking weighs.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks slide further, profit-taking weighs.

text.p: Mexican stocks were showing sharp losses Monday as a morning slump extended into midafternoon.
Dealers said profit-taking on key blue chips weighed heavily on a market whose volume had thinned amid caution prompted by last week's volatility in Brazilian equities.
"We're seeing some continued profit-taking after the strong gains chalked up over the past two months," a desk trader said.
The leading IPC share index was down 107.76 points, or 2.28 percent, at 4,812.80.
Trading volume of 28.5 million shares was much lighter in many recent sessions.

"The Brazilian market is quiet today, but still volatile and markets across Latin America are cautious," the trader said. The Bovespa index of most active stocks in Sao Paulo, zigzagging during most of Monday's session, was down 0.19 percent at 11,160 points.
In Mexico, Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex) led the retreat. Telmex accounted for a quarter of all shares traded and was down 46 centavos at 19.44 pesos.
Dealers said Telmex ADRs, down 15/16 at 49-3/8, had fallen more by a greater extent than the Dow Jones Industrial Average, which was off about nine points at 7,881.
"Telmex would seem to be declining on a disappointing outlook for its second-quarter earnings," the desk trader said.
On the broad market, declining issues outnumbered gainers by 58 to 11, out of a total of 82 stocks changing hands.
